verses.1: For the leader; a psalm with stringed instruments. A song of Asaph.
verses.2: Renowned in Judah is God, whose name is great in Israel.
verses.3: On Salem is God's tent, a shelter on Zion.
verses.4: There the flashing arrows were shattered, shield, sword, and weapons of war. Selah
verses.5: Terrible and awesome are you, stronger than the ancient mountains.
verses.6: Despoiled are the bold warriors; they sleep their final sleep; the hands of all the mighty have failed.
verses.7: At your roar, O God of Jacob, chariots and steeds lay still.
verses.8: So terrible and awesome are you; who can stand before you and your great anger?
verses.9: From the heavens you pronounced sentence; the earth was terrified and reduced to silence,
verses.10: When you arose, O God, for judgment to deliver the afflicted of the land. Selah
verses.11: Even wrathful Edom praises you; the remnant of Hamath keeps your feast.
verses.12: Make and keep vows to the LORD your God. May all present bring gifts to this awesome God,
verses.13: Who checks the pride of princes, inspires awe among the kings of earth.

notes.text: Salem: an ancient name for Jerusalem, used here perhaps on account of its allusion to the Hebrew word for peace, shalom. Cf Genesis 14:18; Hebrews 7:1-3.
Ancient mountains: conjectural translation of a difficult Hebrew phrase on the basis of Genesis 49:26. The mountains are part of the structure of the universe (Psalm 89:12-13).
Edom... Hamath: conjectural translation. Israel's neighbors to the southeast and north.
